data-emphasis.purpose: The port counter's live readout only; the one number the instrument makes loud, with text-shadow glow and a counter-tick pulse on change.

wordmark.purpose: The 'localhub' brand mark in the fascia.

data.purpose: Every port/protocol/PID/process/status value inside a keycap row.

label.purpose: Column headers, counter caption, kill-key legend, status chip text.

shadows.name: panel-ambient
shadows.purpose: Resting depth for the fascia and instrument-panel structural containers.

shadows.name: key-lift
shadows.value: inset 0 1px 0 var(--key-highlight), inset 0 -1px 0 var(--key-shadow); filter: drop-shadow(0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.3))
shadows.purpose: Every port row at rest, reading as a physically raised keycap.

shadows.name: bezel-recess
shadows.purpose: Inset display windows: port counter tube, recessed controls.

shadows.name: kill-key-rest
shadows.purpose: Kill-key resting state, simulating physical key thickness.

motion.name: counter-tick
motion.value: 260ms ease-out, opacity 0.35->1, text-shadow glow intensifies then settles
motion.purpose: Amber digit pulse when the open-port count changes.

motion.name: cool-down-fade
motion.value: 320ms ease, opacity/grayscale/scale(0.98); coordinated with COOL_DOWN_MS = 340 in App.tsx
motion.purpose: Mesophotic Deep Dive raise: a killed row dims and shrinks out instead of vanishing abruptly.

motion.name: refresh-spin
motion.purpose: Refresh knob icon spin while a port list reload is in flight.

motion.name: kill-key-press
motion.purpose: Kill-key travel and shadow collapse on hover/active.

breakpoints.name: row-reflow
breakpoints.purpose: Below this width, port rows switch from a table row to a named CSS grid reflowing whole fields onto two lines.

components.name: Kill Key
components.description: The one committed danger action per port row; orange gradient with a genuine skeuomorphic press.
components.css: .ds-kill-key { font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 7px 13px; border: none; border-radius: 5px; color: #fff3ee; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #ff7648, #ff5a2e); box-shadow: 0 2px 0 #d6431c, 0 3px 5px rgba(0,0,0,0.35); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 100ms ease, box-shadow 100ms ease, background 100ms ease; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-kill-key:hover { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #ff8259, #ff7648); } .ds-kill-key:active { transform: translateY(2px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 #d6431c, 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.35); } .ds-kill-key:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffb238; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-kill-key:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; color: #86887f; background: #1c1f24; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); }

components.name: Refresh Knob
components.description: Knurled circular refresh control beside the port counter; spins its icon while loading.
components.html: <button class="ds-refresh-btn" aria-label="Atualizar"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M3.5 12a8.5 8.5 0 0 1 14.5-6"/><path d="M20.5 12a8.5 8.5 0 0 1-14.5 6"/><path d="M18 6.5V3.5h-3"/><path d="M6 17.5v3h3"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-refresh-btn { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; padding: 0; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1); background: repeating-conic-gradient(from 0deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.05) 0deg 4deg, rgba(255,255,255,0) 4deg 8deg), #1c1f24; color: #92948f; cursor: pointer; transition: color 120ms ease, transform 120ms ease, box-shadow 120ms ease; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.4); } .ds-refresh-btn:hover { color: #e9e6df; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-refresh-btn:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-refresh-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffb238; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Chip (default)
components.description: Recessed pill chip showing a port's state value.
components.css: .ds-status-chip { display: inline-block; max-width: 100%; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.03em; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; background: #1c1f24; color: #92948f; }

components.name: Status Chip (LISTEN)
components.description: The live-status amber variant, used only when a port is actively LISTENing.
components.css: .ds-status-chip-listen { display: inline-block; font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.03em; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; background: #1c1f24; color: #ffb238; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,178,56,0.16); }

components.name: Port Row
components.description: The signature keycap-styled row: one physical key per open port, with mono data values, a status chip, and a kill key.
components.css: .ds-port-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; background: #d9d2c3; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.65), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(35,26,12,0.16); filter: drop-shadow(0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.3)); border-radius: 8px; padding: 11px 14px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; color: #2a2822; } .ds-port-row:hover { background: #e1dbcd; } .ds-port-row__port { font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-port-row__protocol { color: #554f44; font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }

components.name: Port Counter
components.description: Amber glass-tube readout of the live open-port count, with rib-mesh texture and a counter-tick pulse on change.
components.css: .ds-port-counter { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 5px 12px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.03) 0px, rgba(255,255,255,0.03) 1px, transparent 1px, transparent 4px), #1c1f24; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1); border-radius: 5px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); overflow: hidden; } .ds-port-counter__value { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.05rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #ffb238; text-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(255,178,56,0.45); } .ds-port-counter__label { font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.6rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #86887f; }

narrative.overview: localhub is an instrument built by someone who makes their own tools, not a SaaS admin panel. It renders every open port as a physical key on a dark, machined instrument case: a gunmetal chassis holds a grid of raised bone-colored keycaps, an amber glass-tube counter reads the live port count, and one loud safety-orange key is the sole way to end a process. The voice is precise, technical, tactile, and has zero ceremony — nothing slow, decorated, or gamified, and nothing borrowed from the generic soft-shadow/gradient-blue SaaS-admin-dashboard default. This is also not a warm/bookish/cream world: the case reads cool and machined; the only warmth in the system is the keycap material itself and the orange/amber accents. This is a code-led build (no comp/image round; the direction contract's assigned oscilloscope/lab-panel form lost a direction-roll fusion to the 'creator hardware bench' challenger, which is what shipped). Three raises are load-bearing, not decoration: the Nixie Laboratory Counter glow-and-mesh treatment on the port count, the Exposure Record hatch texture marking protected rows (never color alone), and the Mesophotic cool-down fade (COOL_DOWN_MS = 340) that lets a killed row dim out instead of vanishing abruptly.
keyCharacteristics: Dark gunmetal chassis holding light, physically raised keycap rows — layered and lifted, never flat.
One safety-orange kill/danger role, spent only on the kill key and the error alert.
One instrument-amber live-status role, spent only on the port counter and the LISTEN chip.
IBM Plex Mono for every data value (port, protocol, PID, status); IBM Plex Sans for all chrome and copy, set in Brazilian Portuguese.
Whole-row grid reflow on narrow viewports — never a fractional or broken table.

rules.name: The One Loud Key Rule
rules.body: Safety Orange appears in exactly two places system-wide (kill key, error alert) and nowhere else. Its rarity is what makes it read as consequential.

rules.name: The Bezel-Is-a-Window Rule
rules.body: Any small recessed/inset display — a counter, a status readout, a disabled control — draws from the same --bezel token. Don't invent a second dark inset shade.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono marks a live value read off the system; IBM Plex Sans marks everything the interface itself is saying. Never swap the two.

rules.name: The Raised-Key Rule
rules.body: A port row is never flat-filled; it always carries the highlight/shadow pairing plus the row-level drop-shadow. A flat table row is a regression to the pre-ship 'plain HTML table' the direction contract explicitly refused.

dos: Do keep Safety Orange to exactly the kill key and the error alert — one 'kill/danger' role, not a general accent.
Do mark protected/disabled rows with the diagonal hatch texture, never with color alone.
Do use IBM Plex Mono for every value read off the live system (port, protocol, PID, process, status) and IBM Plex Sans for everything the interface says.
Do give every pressable control (kill-key, refresh knob) real travel — a shadow collapse and/or translateY on :active, not a flat color-only hover.
Do reflow narrow layouts by whole field groups via named CSS grid areas, never by letting columns shrink into a broken fractional table.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color outside the orange (kill/danger) and amber (live-status) roles.
Don't flatten a port row to a single background fill — it must carry the highlight/shadow key-lift pairing plus the row-level drop-shadow.
Don't revert to a plain HTML table look or a generic soft-shadow/gradient-blue admin-dashboard treatment; both are explicitly refused by the direction contract this system was built against.
Don't translate interface copy out of Brazilian Portuguese; it is the product's permanent voice, not a placeholder.
